Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The procurement team is reviewing Redwood's RFP response and asked for a few clarifications around Section 4 (Risk Allocation). Attached is the specific excerpt from our RFP questionnaire. Two quick asks: 1) Please confirm whether Redwood requests IP assignment for customer prompts or derivatives, and 2) confirm the proposed liability cap and whether it is tied to the Order Form fees or a fixed dollar amount.

We also saw a placeholder about indemnity for IP infringement and wanted to know whether that is one-way (vendor-only) or mutual. Could you send a short written response we can include with our buyer-side legal review?

Best,

Subject: Re: Clarification: RFP Section 4 (Risk Allocation) - IP / Indemnity / Cap

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the clear note and the attached excerpt. Quick responses inline below and we've attached a short draft we typically share with customers for procurement/legal. High level:

- IP: Redwood does not claim ownership of customer prompts or customer-provided data. We license models and software to customers; derivatives generated from customer prompts are treated per the terms in the Order Form. We will confirm specific language suggested by legal.

- Indemnity: Our standard is vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement that arises from our services (e.g., model weights/providers where we represent rights), plus a mutual carve-out for customer data-related claims. We'll send the standard clause but welcome negotiation.

- Liability cap: We typically propose the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months under the Order Form, or (b) a fixed floor of $200,000 for enterprise pilots; for larger enterprise commitments we escalate the cap with negotiated SOW/order value. We can tie the cap explicitly to the Order Form.

Attached: Redwood_response_risk_alloc_draft.docx (contains suggested language and a short rationale).

I looped in Aditya to help with commercial context / commitment size so we can align the cap to the expected Order Form value. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if that keeps things moving.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-08-14T11:55:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FW: Clarification: RFP Section 4 (Risk Allocation) - proposed language

Evelyn / Aditya – below is suggested language and negotiation guidance. I attached a redline of the Order Form schedule with the cap tied to Order Form fees and a small fixed-dollar floor. Key points:

1) IP: Proposed statement – "Customer retains all rights, title and interest in Customer Data and Customer Content (including prompts and prompt-derived outputs). Redwood retains rights in its pre-existing models, software and tools. No assignment of Customer IP is required."

2) IP Indemnity: Proposed indemnity – "Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer from third-party claims alleging that Redwood's services infringe a third party's intellectual property, subject to Customer's prompt notice and reasonable cooperation. This indemnity does not apply to infringement arising from Customer Data or Customer's modifications or combination with non-Redwood materials."

3) Liability Cap: Two recommended, clear options to propose in negotiation:
   - Option A (standard enterprise): Cap = greater of (i) fees paid under the Order Form in the prior 12 months, or (ii) $250,000.
   - Option B (large commitments): Cap = higher of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months, or (ii) $1,000,000 — for Order Forms with annual committed spend > $5M or where SLA credits are material.

4) Carve-outs (recommended): We propose the following carve-outs from the cap: (i) willful misconduct or gross negligence; (ii) Redwood's indemnity obligations for IP infringement; (iii) obligations arising under privacy/data breach where Redwood's breach of its security obligations caused the loss. Keep carve-outs narrow to avoid unlimited exposure.

5) Order Form linkage: I redlined the Order Form risk schedule to reference "cap shall be set per the Order Form (Section X)." That lets commercial pick a cap tier at signature without changing base T&Cs.

Next steps: I recommend sending procurement a short packet (1 page summary + attached redline). If procurement insists on assignment or unlimited liability for data, escalate to execs. I'm flexible on the floor values; Aditya, confirm the likely initial ARR and we'll pick Option A or B.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah,

Appreciate the patience. Attached is a concise packet for procurement/legal: (1) one-page summary of Redwood's position, (2) redline to the Order Form risk schedule, and (3) suggested indemnity/IP language. High-level answers for your legal team:

- IP: Customer retains rights in Customer Data and outputs derived from its prompts. Redwood retains model and software rights; no IP assignment requested.
- Indemnity: We propose vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement (with standard notice/cooperation requirements). Exclusions apply where the claim is based on customer data or customer modifications.
- Liability Cap: We propose the cap be set in the Order Form. For initial sizing, our standard enterprise default is the greater of (a) prior 12 months' fees or (b) $250,000. For larger commitments we offer higher tiers (e.g., $1M) tied to contract value. Carve-outs for IP indemnity and willful misconduct are included in the redline.

If those high-level positions look acceptable, can we schedule a 20-minute call early next week to walk procurement through the rationale and land final language? I can have Marissa or one of our counsel join on the call if procurement wants to push redlines.

Thanks again — we want to keep momentum and get a clean order form so NovaPower can start the pilot.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
